Since \(\mathcal{F}\) is a sheaf, it suffices to verify this after replacing \(\mu\) by the various objects of one of its coverings; by (\(\mathcal{L}\)2), this allows us to assume the diagrams analogous to the preceding one, with \(\lambda^2\) replaced by \(\lambda^1\), likewise commutative, in which case the assertion is obvious.

(ii) Let \(f : U \longrightarrow V\) in \(\mathcal{A}^*\), \(\lambda \in \operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}^*_U\), and \(\mu \in \operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}^*_V\). There then exists a covering \(f_j : U_j \longrightarrow U\), an object \(\mu' \in \operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}^*_U\), and arrows \[ \xymatrix@R=2em@C=3em{ \lambda_j \ar[r]^-{\phi_j} \ar[d]_-{\psi_j} & \lambda \\ \mu \ar[r]_-{\psi} & \mu' } \] over \[ \xymatrix@C=3em{U_j \ar[r]^-{f_j} & U \ar[r]^-{f} & V} \]

By (i), there exists one and only one arrow \(\bar{f}\) making the following diagram commutative: \[ \xymatrix@R=2em@C=3em{ \mathcal{F}(\mu) \ar[r]^-{\bar{f}} \ar[d]_-{\phi} & \mathcal{F}(\lambda) \ar[d]^-{\phi_j} \\ \mathcal{F}(\mu') \ar[r]_-{\psi_j} & \mathcal{F}(\lambda_j) } \] The arrow \(\bar{f}\) does not change when we replace \((f_j)\) by a finer covering given by \(f_k : U_k \longrightarrow U_{j(k)}\), replace \(\lambda_j\) by \(\lambda_k\), equipped with \(\phi_k \in \operatorname{Hom}_{f_k}(\lambda_k, \lambda_{j(k)})\), and replace \(\phi_j(\psi_j)\) by \(\phi_{j(k)} \circ \phi_k\) (\(\psi_{j(k)} \circ \phi_k\)).
We leave it to the reader to deduce that \(\bar{f}\) depends only on \(f\).

(iii) Let us prove that \(\bar{f}\) is functorial in \(f\). Let then \[ \xymatrix@C=3em{W \ar[r]^-{h} & V \ar[r]^-{g} & U} \] be in \(\mathcal{A}\) and \(\lambda^\circ, \mu^\circ, \nu^\circ\) in \(\operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}_U\), \(\operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}_V\), and \(\operatorname{Ob} \mathcal{A}_W\) respectively. There exists a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix@R=1.8em@C=2em{ & \nu^\circ \ar[r] & \mu^\circ \ar[r] & \lambda^\circ \\ \nu^1 \ar[ur] & & & \\ \nu^2 \ar[u] & & \mu_j \ar[uur]_-{f_j^i} & \\ & \nu_{jk} \ar[ul] \ar[uul]^-{e_{jk}^i} \ar[ur] & & } \] such that
b) with \(i\) fixed, the \(e_{jk}^i\) cover \(W\) and the \(f_j^i\) cover \(V\).

We first construct \(\mu^1\), \(\nu^1\), and \(\nu^2\) by (\(\mathcal{L}\)0), and the \(\mu_j\) as in (ii). Let \(W'_{jk}\) be a covering of \(W\) mapping into the covering \(V_j = t^*(\mu_j)\) as required for the diagram. Refining \(W'_{jk}\) and applying (\(\mathcal{L}\)0) and (\(\mathcal{L}\)1), we obtain a diagram not necessarily commutative, of the required type, satisfying a) and b). Refining further and applying (\(\mathcal{L}\)2), we make it commutative.

It remains then to contemplate the following commutative diagram: \[ \xymatrix@R=2em@C=2.5em{ \mathcal{F}(\lambda^\circ) \ar[r]^-{\bar{g}} & \mathcal{F}(\mu^\circ) \ar[r]^-{\bar{h}} \ar[d] & \mathcal{F}(\nu^\circ) \ar[d] \\ \mathcal{F}(\mu^1) \ar[r] & \prod \mathcal{F}(\mu_j) \ar[r] & \mathcal{F}(\nu^1) \ar[d] \\ \mathcal{F}(\nu^2) \ar[rr] & & \prod \mathcal{F}(\nu_{jk}) } \]

(iv) It is clear that \(\bar{g}\) is functorial in \(\mathcal{F}\): every sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(\mathcal{A}^*\) is therefore the direct image under \(t\) of a (uniquely determined) presheaf \(\mathcal{F}_0\) on \(\mathcal{A}\), and every morphism of sheaves \(f : \mathcal{F} \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}\) is the image of one and only one morphism of presheaves \(f_0 : \mathcal{F}_0 \longrightarrow \mathcal{G}_0\).

It already follows that \(t_*\) is fully faithful; it remains to prove that \(\mathcal{F}_0\) is a sheaf. If \(f_j : U_j \longrightarrow U\) is a covering, this covering is the image of a covering in \(\mathcal{A}^*\), so that \(\mathcal{F}_0(U)\) injects into \(\prod_j \mathcal{F}_0(U_j)\). If elements \(x_j \in \mathcal{F}_0(U_j)\) glue, then, a fortiori, they glue in \(\mathcal{A}^*\) and hence come from an element of \(\mathcal{F}_0(U)\). This completes the proof of (8.1.12).

Let \(q : \mathcal{C} \longrightarrow \mathcal{B}\), \(p : \mathcal{L} \longrightarrow \mathcal{B}\), and \(\mathcal{L}^*\) be as in (8.1.10), and \(\mathcal{D}\) a stack on \(\mathcal{C}\). The stack \(q_* \mathcal{D}\) on \(\mathcal{B}\) is the stack "defined" by \((q_* \mathcal{D})_U = \mathcal{D}_{q^* U}\).

If \((X_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}}\) is a local projective system indexed by \(\mathcal{L}\) with values in \(q_* \mathcal{D}\), we define a local projective system indexed by \(\mathcal{L}^*\) and with values in \(\mathcal{D} : (X_L)_{L \in \mathcal{L}^*}\) by the formula \[ X_L = \phi^* X_\lambda \quad \text{for } L = (V, U, \phi, \lambda) . \] We leave it to the reader to verify that:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.1.13.1

With the preceding notation, we have \[ \varprojlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} X_\lambda \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \varprojlim_{L \in \mathcal{L}^*} X_L , \] the two sides being simultaneously defined or not.

Let \(\mathcal{B}\) be a site and \(p^* : \mathcal{B}^* \longrightarrow \mathcal{B}\) a locally filtered category over \(\mathcal{B}\). If \(\mathcal{C}\) is a stack on \(\mathcal{B}\), then \(p_* \mathcal{C}\) is a stack on \(\mathcal{B}^*\) (8.1.13.0); moreover, the identity functor \(\mathcal{B}^* \longrightarrow \mathcal{B}^*\) is a locally filtered category over \(\mathcal{B}^*\), equipped with the induced topology, and every local inductive system \((X_\lambda)\) indexed by \(\mathcal{B}^*\) defines a local inductive system, indexed by \(\mathcal{B}^*\), on \(\mathcal{B}^*\).
One easily verifies:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.1.14

With the preceding notation, we have \[ \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{B}^*/\mathcal{B}} X_\lambda = \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{B}^*/\mathcal{B}^*} X_\lambda , \] the two sides being simultaneously defined or not.
8.2. Local inductive limits in categories of sheaves
Let \(p : T \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism of sites. Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be the following stack on \(S\)
(i) An object of \(\mathcal{C}\) is a pair \((U, \mathcal{F})\) consisting of an object of \(S\) and a sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(p^* U\).

(ii) An arrow \(f : (U, \mathcal{F}) \longrightarrow (V, \mathcal{G})\) is a pair consisting of an arrow \(f_0 : U \longrightarrow V\) and a morphism of \(T/U\)-sheaves: \[ f_1 : p^*(f_0)^* \mathcal{G} \longrightarrow \mathcal{F} \]
(iii) The functor from \(\mathcal{C}\) to \(S\) is given by \(f \longmapsto f_0\).
Note carefully that \(\mathcal{C}_U\) is the opposite category of the category of sheaves on \(p^* U\).
Let \(\mathcal{L}\) be a locally left-cofiltered category over \(S\).

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition 8.2.1

With the preceding notation, the category of local inductive systems, indexed by \(\mathcal{L}\), of sheaves on \(T\), is the category \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{C})^\circ\).

The "projective limit" functor of 8.1.3 is here called the "local inductive limit" functor. It is a functor from \(\operatorname{Hom}_S(\mathcal{L}, \mathcal{C})^\circ\) to \((\Gamma\mathcal{C})^\circ = \widetilde{T}\).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 8.2.2

The "local inductive limit" functor from the category of inductive systems of sheaves on \(T\), indexed by \(\mathcal{L}\), to the category of sheaves on \(T\), is everywhere defined, commutes with finite projective limits, and commutes with arbitrary inductive limits.

Propositions 8.1.13, 8.1.14, and 8.1.12 allow us to reduce to the case where \(S = T = \mathcal{L}\). A local inductive system is then given, for each \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S\), by a sheaf \(\mathcal{F}_U\) on \(S_{/U}\), and, for each arrow \(f : V \longrightarrow U\) in \(S\), by an arrow, functorial in \(f\), from \(f^* \mathcal{F}_U\) to \(\mathcal{F}_V\).
For such inductive systems, the \(\varinjlim\) are computed as follows:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 8.2.3

Let \(U \longmapsto \mathcal{F}_U\) be a section of the category of presheaves over the objects of \(S\). We have \[ a(U \longmapsto \Gamma(U, \mathcal{F}_U)) \simeq \varinjlim_U a \mathcal{F}_U \]

By definition, the right-hand side represents the functor which, to each sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(S\), associates the set of coherent systems of arrows \(\phi_U : \mathcal{F}_U \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}|U\). In turn, an arrow \(\phi_U\) is a coherent system of arrows \(\phi_g\), one for each \(g : V \longrightarrow U\), \(\phi_g : \mathcal{F}_U(V) \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}(V)\). Let us apply 8.1.11 to the identity functor of \(S\), thus obtaining \(S^*\) locally filtered over \(S\). We have seen that \[ \varinjlim_{g \in S} \mathcal{F}_U(V_g)^\sim \simeq \varinjlim_U a \mathcal{F}_U , \] where \(V_g\) is the source of \(g\) and \(\sim\) is the "generated constant sheaf" functor. The functor \(U \longmapsto 1_U\) from \(S\) to \(S^*\) is cofinal, whence again by 8.1.5 \[ \varinjlim_U \mathcal{F}_U(U)^\sim \simeq \varinjlim_U a \mathcal{F}_U . \] Returning to the definitions, we finally find \[ \varinjlim_U \mathcal{F}_U(U)^\sim \simeq a (U \longmapsto \Gamma(U, \mathcal{F}_U)) . \] This shows that in the case to which we have reduced, the functor \(\varinjlim\) is everywhere defined, and that it is computed as the composite of the "sheaf generated by a presheaf" functor and the functor \((\mathcal{F}_U) \longmapsto (U \longmapsto \Gamma(U, \mathcal{F}_U))\). These two functors commute with finite projective limits, and the functor \(\varinjlim\) moreover commutes with arbitrary inductive limits by virtue of its definition as an adjoint functor.

Lemma 8.2.3 provides a systematic procedure for proving properties of the local inductive limit functor from analogous properties of the "sheaf associated to a presheaf" functor. In this way one finds:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.2.4

Let \(T\), \(S\), and \(\mathcal{L}\) be as before, \(\mathcal{A}_\lambda\) a local inductive system of rings on \(T\), \(\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) (resp. \(\mathcal{M}_\lambda\)) a local inductive system of sheaves of right (resp. left) modules over \(\mathcal{A}_\lambda\), all three indexed by \(\mathcal{L}\). We have \[ \varinjlim_\lambda (\mathcal{L}_\lambda \otimes_{\mathcal{A}_\lambda} \mathcal{M}_\lambda) = \varinjlim_\lambda \mathcal{L}_\lambda \otimes_{\varinjlim_\lambda \mathcal{A}_\lambda} \varinjlim_\lambda \mathcal{M}_\lambda . \]
(Reduce to the case \(T = S = \mathcal{L}\), and note that the two sides coincide with the sheaf generated by the presheaf of \[ \mathcal{L}_U(U) \otimes_{\mathcal{A}_U(U)} \mathcal{M}_U(U) ) . \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.2.5

Let \(T_1 \overset{q}{\longrightarrow} T_2 \longrightarrow S\) be two morphisms of sites, and \((F_\lambda)\) a local inductive system of sheaves on \(T_2\) indexed by a locally cofiltered category \(\mathcal{L}\) over \(S\). We have \[ q^* \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} F_\lambda \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} q^* F_\lambda . \]
This follows immediately from the fact that \(q^*\) admits a right adjoint \(q_*\).

Let \(S\) and \(T\) be two sites in which the finite \(\varprojlim\) are representable, let \(p : T \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism of sites such that \(p^* : S \longrightarrow T\) commutes with finite \(\varprojlim\), and let \(\mathcal{L}\) be the locally cofiltered category over \(T\) having as objects the triples \((V, U, \phi)\) where \(V \in \operatorname{Ob} T\), \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S\), and \(\phi \in \operatorname{Hom}(V, p^* U)\). We obtain it by applying 8.1.11 to \(1_S : S \longrightarrow S\).

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.2.6

For every sheaf \(\mathcal{F}\) on \(T\), we have \[ \mathcal{F} = \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} \phi^* \phi_* \mathcal{F} \] where, by abuse of notation, \(\phi\) denotes the morphism induced by \(p\) from \(T/V\) to \(S/U\).

Let \(\phi'\) be the inverse image functor in the sense of presheaves; from 8.2.3, we deduce \[ \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} \phi^* \phi_* \mathcal{F} = \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} a \phi' \phi_* \mathcal{F} = \varinjlim_{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}} \mathcal{F}(V)^\sim = \mathcal{F} . \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 8.2.7

Let \(p : T \longrightarrow S\) be a morphism of topoi, \(\mathcal{O}_S\) a sheaf of rings on \(S\), and \(\mathcal{O}_T\) its inverse image on \(T\). For a right \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-Module \(\mathcal{M}\) to be flat over \(\mathcal{O}_T\), it is necessary and sufficient that the functor \[ (8.2.7.1) \qquad \mathcal{N} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} p^* \mathcal{N} \] from the category of left \(\mathcal{O}_S\)-Modules to that of abelian sheaves on \(T\) be exact.
The "necessary" assertion is trivial; let us therefore suppose the functor (8.2.7.1) exact, and prove that \(\mathcal{M}\) is flat.

We can assume \(p\) is defined by a morphism of sites \(p : T \longrightarrow S\) satisfying the hypotheses made in 2.6. Let \(V \in \operatorname{Ob} T\), \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S\), and \(\phi : V \longrightarrow p^* U\). We again denote by \(\phi\) the induced morphism of sites: \(\phi : T/V \longrightarrow S/U\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 8.2.8

The functor \(\mathcal{N} \longmapsto \mathcal{M}|V \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_V} \phi^* \mathcal{N}\), from the category of \(\mathcal{O}_S|U\)-modules on \(S/U\) to that of \(\mathcal{O}_T|V\)-modules on \(T/V\), is exact.

We reduce to taking \(V = p^* U\). Let \(j\) and \(j'\) be the "inclusion morphisms": \(j : S/U \longrightarrow S\) and \(j' : T/p^* U \longrightarrow T\). We have: \[ j'_!(\mathcal{M}|V \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_V} \phi^* \mathcal{N}) = \mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} p^* j_! \mathcal{N} , \] whence 8.2.8, since \(j_!\) and \(j'_!\) are exact and faithful.

Let then \(Q\) be an \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-Module. We have (8.2.6) \[ Q = \varinjlim_{\phi : V \to p^* U} \phi^* \phi_* Q|V \] so that (8.2.4) \[ \mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} Q = \varinjlim_{\phi : V \to p^* U} \mathcal{M}|V \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_V} \phi^* \phi_* Q|V \] By 8.2.8, the functors \(Q \longmapsto \mathcal{M}|V \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_V} \phi^* \phi_* Q|V\) are left exact, so that \(\mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} Q\) is left exact in \(Q\), hence exact.

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 8.2.9

Let \(f : (T, \mathcal{O}_T) \longrightarrow (S, \mathcal{O}_S)\) be a morphism of ringed topoi. Then the inverse image under \(f\) of a sheaf of flat (right) modules is a sheaf of flat modules.

Factoring \(f\) through \((T, f^* \mathcal{O}_S)\), we reduce to the case \(\mathcal{O}_T = f^* \mathcal{O}_S\). Let then \(\mathcal{M}\) be a sheaf of flat modules on \(S\). By 8.2.7, to check that \(f^* \mathcal{M}\) is flat, it suffices to check the exactness of the functor \[ \mathcal{N} \longmapsto f^* \mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_T} f^* \mathcal{N} = f^*(\mathcal{M} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathcal{N}) \] whence the assertion, since \(f^*\) is exact.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 8.2.10

Let \((S, \mathcal{O}_S)\) be a ringed topos, \(\mathcal{F}\) a sheaf of left modules locally of finite presentation, \(\mathcal{G}\) a sheaf of bimodules, and \(\mathcal{H}\) a flat sheaf of left modules. Then the canonical arrow \[ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) \otimes \mathcal{H} \longrightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G} \otimes \mathcal{H}) \] is an isomorphism.

The question is local on \(S\), which allows us to assume that \(\mathcal{F}\) admits a finite presentation \[ \mathcal{F}_1 \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}_0 \longrightarrow \mathcal{F} \longrightarrow 0 \] The first row of the following diagram is exact, since \(\mathcal{H}\) is flat: \[ \xymatrix@R=2.5em@C=1.6em{ 0 \ar[r] & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) \otimes \mathcal{H} \ar[r] \ar[d] & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{G}) \otimes \mathcal{H} \ar[r] \ar[d]^-{S} & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_2, \mathcal{G}) \otimes \mathcal{H} \ar[d]^-{S} \\ 0 \ar[r] & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G} \otimes \mathcal{H}) \ar[r] & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{G} \otimes \mathcal{H}) \ar[r] & \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal{F}_2, \mathcal{G} \otimes \mathcal{H}) } \] whence the assertion. Taking \(\mathcal{G} = \mathcal{A}\), we deduce from 8.2.10:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 8.2.11

Every morphism from a sheaf of modules locally of finite presentation to a sheaf of flat modules factors, locally on \(S\), through a free sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_S^n\) (\(n \in \mathbf{N}\)).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 8.2.12 (D. Lazard)

For a sheaf of modules \(\mathcal{M}\) on a ringed site \((S, \mathcal{O}_S)\) to be flat, it is necessary and sufficient that it be a local inductive limit of free modules of finite type.
The "sufficiency" follows from 8.2.2, 8.2.4.

For every \(U \in \operatorname{Ob} S\), let \(\mathcal{L}_0(U)\) (resp. \(\mathcal{L}_1(U)\)) be the category of sheaves of free modules of finite type (resp. of finite presentation) on \(U\), equipped with a linear map to \(\mathcal{M}|U\). For every arrow \(f : V \longrightarrow U\) in \(S\), let \(f^*\) be the restriction functor from \(\mathcal{L}_i(U)\) to \(\mathcal{L}_i(V)\). These functors define a category \(\mathcal{L}_i\), fibred over \(S\), whose fibres are the opposite categories of the categories \(\mathcal{L}_i(U)\).

The reader will verify that the category \(\mathcal{L}_1\) is locally filtered over \(S\), and that \[ \mathcal{M} = \varinjlim_{(M, f) \in \mathcal{L}_1} M \] If \(\mathcal{M}\) is flat, the inclusion of \(\mathcal{L}_0\) in \(\mathcal{L}_1\) is fully faithful and, by 8.2.11, satisfies (C\(\mathcal{F}\)1) of 8.1.4. It then automatically satisfies (C\(\mathcal{F}\)2), and \(\mathcal{L}_0\) is locally filtered. By 8.1.5, we have \[ \mathcal{M} = \varinjlim_{(M, f) \in \mathcal{L}_0} M , \] whence the assertion 8.2.12.
